France-United States Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (1967, as amended)
France-United Kingdom Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (2008)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each shareholder/managing director
Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement) for each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or bank institution in country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of corporate registration certificate and bylaws for each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Trade registry or equivalent authority of country of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing for each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, shareholders, and senior managers against the French national sanctions lists (Fichier National des Comptes Irréguliers et Sanctions), European Union consolidated financial sanctions lists, United Nations Security Council sanctions lists, OFAC SDN list, and internal risk-rating algorithms. Additional Enhanced Due Diligence required for any PEP or PEP-family relationship, or for dealings involving high-risk third-country jurisdictions as defined by FATF.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) / INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle) for trademark screening; Infogreffe for commercial registration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in French, or in a language compatible with the usage of international trade. If transliterated from a non-Latin script, a French version must be submitted for registration. The name must be distinct from all existing French company names and shall not be false, misleading, or contrary to public policy. The use of any translation of the specified business purpose (clear dental aligners) is permitted.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In the event the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce rejects the proposed name, the applicant may file an administrative review with the same registry within one month of the rejection, accompanied by supporting evidence of distinctiveness. If rejected again, an appeal may be submitted to the President of the competent Commercial Court within one month. Additionally, the applicant may simultaneously reserve the desired name as a trademark with INPI to establish prior rights, and such reservation is valid for 10 years and can be used as evidence in the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are permissible for SARL companies in France, provided the registered office is situated in the company's principal place of administration or at a law-abiding business domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) that holds a valid administrative declaration. For the clear aligner production/importation activity, a physical commercial presence (warehouse or production facility) is not strictly necessary for incorporation, but will be required if the company intends to perform physical thermoforming operations locally; virtual office is only acceptable for administrative seat purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium (approximately 35% risk over the first 24 months) – the ACPR and social fiscal authorities may conduct unannounced inspections based on sectoral risk, but for a low-risk dental device company with fully documented substance, the chance is reduced to around 20%. If a virtual office is chosen without any local operational footprint, the risk rises to 50% owing to economic substance enforcement in Paris and Lyon.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per annexe 3 to Article R123-227, Code de commerce

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce, articles L. 223-1 et seq. (Sociétés à responsabilité limitée)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce du siège social
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum capital social of 1 euro; no escrow account required but capital must be fully paid and verifiable
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the initial capital of the Company is subscribed as follows: the subscriber subscribes for 100% of the shares at a nominal value of 1 euro per share, totaling 1 euro. The registered office is adopted at [full French address]. The following officers are appointed: [Name] as Président, [Name] as gérant, and [Name] as directeur. The Articles of Association are adopted in the form provided. The Company is authorized to open bank accounts and perform all acts of incorporation and operation. This resolution is adopted unanimously by the sole shareholder and initial director.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Filing of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via guichet-entreprises or infogreffe.com portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Association in French language detailing share capital, object, directors, and registered office. Have all shareholders sign. Submit online or in person at the greffe with identity documents, proof of registered office, and any applicable fees. The greffe registers the company and issues the SIREN and SIRET numbers.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Provide additional information or documents within the deadline if the application is queried or incomplete

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Agence Nationale de Sécurité du Médicament et des Produits de Santé (ANSM)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation de fabrication de dispositifs médicaux (Manufacturing Authorization for Medical Devices)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition écologique et de la Cohésion des territoires
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with French environmental regulations for plastic processing, VOC emissions, and medical waste handling per EU directives

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification, structural safety inspections, and workplace health and safety clearance from the Préfecture

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des finances publiques (DGFiP); online tax services and filings are administered through impots.gouv.fr. Business formation is filed through the INPI-operated Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Register the SARL through the Guichet unique. The registration process results in assignment of a SIREN and SIRET and entry in the Registre national des entreprises; the company receives its French VAT number when registered for VAT by the competent Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE). A foreign company without a French establishment applies to the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères (SIEE). A non-EU business generally appoints a French fiscal representative unless an applicable legal exemption or mutual-assistance arrangement applies. Confirm the VAT number through the EU VIES system before cross-border use.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SARL is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS). Eligible SARLs may elect income-tax transparency (impôt sur le revenu, IR) for a limited period, generally up to five financial years, subject to statutory conditions. A family-owned SARL conducting an eligible activity may elect IR without that five-year limit while the conditions continue to be met. France has no U.S.-style check-the-box election; the IR election is not automatic and must be made under prescribed procedures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT, taxe sur la valeur ajoutée or TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold exempts a French-established business from VAT registration when it conducts taxable transactions outside the small-business franchise regime. The franchise en base de TVA may apply below the applicable annual thresholds; the general thresholds are EUR 85,000 for supplies of goods and EUR 37,500 for services, subject to statutory tolerance thresholds and current-year legislative changes. A business must assess its activity and applicable rules rather than assume that manufacturing or mixed supplies qualify for the goods threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France does not generally require real-time tax-authority clearance or digital stamping of domestic VAT invoices. The domestic e-invoicing and e-reporting reform is being phased in: businesses must be able to receive electronic invoices from 1 September 2026; issuance and transaction-reporting obligations apply according to the statutory timetable and business size, with the final phase scheduled for 1 September 2027. In-scope invoices must use the prescribed formats and approved platforms or the public invoicing portal, as applicable. Verify implementation dates and platform rules before launch.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched from France to a destination outside the EU may be exempt with credit (effectively 0% VAT) when statutory conditions are met and the supplier retains evidence that the goods left the EU. Intra-EU supplies of goods may be exempt when the customer is VAT-identified in another Member State, the goods are transported there, and reporting and documentary conditions are satisfied. Services are not automatically zero-rated merely because the customer is offshore; place-of-supply rules, customer status, service type, and any applicable exclusions determine treatment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial invoice identifying the goods, parties, VAT treatment, and transaction
Customs confirmation of exit from the EU, such as the electronic exit result or IE599 message where available
Transport evidence, such as bill of lading, air waybill, CMR, or carrier delivery records
Purchase order, payment evidence, and correspondence supporting the transaction and destination
For qualifying intra-EU supplies: customer VAT-number validation, transport evidence, and required recapitulative statement reporting
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The supplier must substantiate the export or other exemption and retain records for the applicable statutory period. If the conditions or evidence are insufficient, the tax authority may reassess VAT, interest, and applicable penalties. Intentional fraud or false documentation may attract enhanced tax penalties and criminal sanctions. France imposes no general 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds; the specified deadline is therefore not applicable.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France operates a regime of full capital and current account convertibility for the Euro. Profit remittances to foreign shareholders are unrestricted following standard corporate tax compliance, beneficial ownership registration under the French Transparency Act, and AML monitoring. No capital controls or material FX transfer hurdles apply to intra-EU or OECD transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds to the central bank. Export receipts must be declared to customs authorities (Douane) within one month of shipment. Companies may retain and utilize proceeds freely after declaration, subject only to standard AML transaction monitoring and reporting thresholds.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. French EMI licensing by ACPR permits cross-border electronic money services within the EEA but imposes strict capital, liquidity, reserve, and AML obligations. Offshore digital EMIs face regulatory barriers for non-EEA activities and require full local compliance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital onboarding is permitted for standard corporate clients via e-KYC, video identification, and biometric verification. Physical appearance of directors is required only for high-risk entities, complex ownership structures, or when regulatory red flags trigger enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source of wealth and source of funds statements, enhanced due diligence reports, senior management approval, and independent compliance audit

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or adverse media screening hits
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive ownership chain documentation, legal entity verification certificates, passport copies, and independent compliance audit
Ultimate beneficial owner declarations under French Transparency Act, address proofs, and tax ID alignment

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocols include SWIFT MT103 transfers with purpose code 'CAP' (capital injection) or 'EQTY' (equity contribution). Verification requires bank reference letters, ownership percentage proofs, tax ID alignment, and French AML reporting. All transactions must comply with threshold-based suspicious activity reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails primarily utilize SWIFT MT103 for international wire transfers and Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) for trade settlements. For dental aligner manufacturing, payments to suppliers or clients follow standard B2B protocols with proper invoice matching, VAT handling, and export/import declarations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and Management Report (Comptes Annuels et Rapport de Gestion)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) via INPI Guichet Electronique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven (7) months of fiscal year-end (31 July for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file is a criminal offence: director fine up to EUR 10,000; administrative injunction with coercive penalty (astreinte) up to EUR 150 per day; may result in civil strike-off or compulsory dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders' Meeting Approval Record (Procès-Verbal de Décisions des Associés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) - deposited together with annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM to be held within six (6) months of fiscal year-end; minutes filed within one (1) month thereafter (i.e., 31 July for 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unfiled minutes invalidate the legal approval of accounts; late filing penalties of EUR 15 per day; may trigger opposition by tax authorities and judicial strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Déclaration de Résultat – Form 2065 series)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year taxpayers, file by the 3rd business day of May (usually 3 May); non-calendar years by 15th day after annual meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% of tax due; after formal notice, 40%; plus monthly interest of 0.20%; potential unilateral tax assessment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Tax on Fixed Assets (Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises – CFE) Declaration and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due 15 December each year; declaration via annual tax return (Form 1327-AC) on the same date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty 10% plus monthly interest 0.20%; enforced recovery from bank accounts or commercial assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO Register Update (Déclaration des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) upon Shareholding Changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership, including share transfers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 15,000; criminal sanction for false declaration up to EUR 37,500 and/or 1 year imprisonment; suspension of voting rights for shareholders in arrears.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (Commissaire aux Comptes) is mandatory for a SARL if two of the following thresholds are exceeded at fiscal year-end: total assets > EUR 4,000,000; net turnover > EUR 8,000,000; average workforce > 50 employees. Also required if the entity controls or is controlled by a company exceeding thresholds, or if shareholders representing 1/3 of capital request (certain criteria).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (French GAAP) per the Plan Comptable Général; compliance with the French Commercial Code (Code de Commerce); mandatory Chart of Accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no standalone annual UBO confirmation filing under French law. However, the beneficial owners must be identified and kept in a continuous register at the registered office; any share transfer or change in control triggers a formal update of the UBO declaration and filing with the INPI/RBE within 30 days. The company must also be able to produce the register of associates and UBO information upon judicial or administrative request.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registre des associés (Register of Members – current and past shareholders, contributions, transfers)
Registre des procès-verbaux des assemblées (Minute Book – records of AGM and shareholders' decisions)
Registre des mouvements de titres (Share Transfer Register – if shares are transferred, approved and recorded)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 – USD 950 per year for professional registered-office or corporate-services agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 – USD 15,000 per year for a statutory audit, when mandated or voluntarily engaged; fees vary with entity complexity and number of transactions

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard rate) plus 3.3% social surcharge on tax exceeding €763,000, yielding an effective top rate of 25.825%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% on the first €42,500 of taxable profit for SMEs with turnover below €10 million; research tax credit (CIR) and innovation tax credit (CII) available for qualifying R&D expenditures

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 (income tax return) and Form 2065-SD (balance sheet and supporting schedules) filed electronically via the EFI (Echange de Formulaires Informatisés) portal at impots.gouv.fr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal year ending 31 December, the filing deadline is the second business day after 1 May. For other fiscal year-ends, the deadline is within 3 months of the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: SIREN, SIRET, legal form, registered office address
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide French tax identification number (obtained via non-resident registration) and permanent establishment address if applicable

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (bénéfice imposable) after deduction of allowable expenses and depreciation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only French-source income attributable to the French permanent establishment; apply treaty provisions if applicable

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits (crédits d'impôt) – e.g., CIC, CII, foreign tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim treaty relief for foreign taxes paid on French-source income; attach Form 2065-SD supporting schedules

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses carried forward (déficits reportables) – amount used in current year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply indefinite carryforward with annual cap of €1 million plus 50% of excess; document loss history

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 10% of tax due, increased to 40% if the return is not filed within 30 days after a formal notice; interest at 0.20% per month on unpaid tax; additional penalties for fraudulent filing (80% of tax due)

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% for non-resident corporate shareholders (unless reduced by tax treaty); 30% flat tax for individual non-residents (unless treaty relief)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must obtain a certificate of residence (Formulaire 5000) from its home tax authority and submit it to the French paying entity before the dividend payment; the paying entity then applies the reduced withholding rate or exemption under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (if holding ≥10% for 2 years). For treaty rates, the beneficiary must provide a completed Form 5001 (attestation de résidence) and supporting documentation to the French tax administration.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: royalties 33.33% (unless treaty reduces); interest 30% (unless treaty reduces). Under most DTAs, royalty rates are reduced to 0-10% and interest to 0-10% depending on the treaty. For EU residents, the Interest and Royalties Directive may provide 0% withholding if conditions are met.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full transfer pricing documentation (Master File and Local File) is mandatory for companies with annual revenue or total assets exceeding €400 million; simplified documentation applies to SMEs with revenue below €400 million but still requires a basic TP file if cross-border transactions exceed €50,000 per category.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not have a specific Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) like the UAE, but the general anti-abuse rule (Article 64 of the French Tax Code) and the doctrine of 'substance over form' apply. The French tax administration may challenge arrangements lacking economic substance, particularly for shell companies or conduit entities. The 'abuse of law' procedure (abus de droit) can recharacterize transactions if the sole purpose is tax avoidance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income, false accounting, or concealment of French-source revenue (e.g., failing to report sales from French customers)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalty of up to €500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years (increased to 7 years for aggravated circumstances); civil penalty of 80% of the evaded tax plus interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes if they have committed fraud or mismanagement; travel bans and asset freezes can be imposed; in severe cases, imprisonment up to 5 years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a letterbox company with no real business activity, no employees, no physical presence, and no substantive decision-making in France, while claiming treaty benefits or routing profits artificially
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of transactions under the abuse of law doctrine; denial of treaty benefits; imposition of 80% penalty on recharacterized amounts; potential criminal charges for tax fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held jointly liable for the company's tax debts if the company is deemed a sham; personal assets may be seized; travel bans and prohibition from managing companies may be imposed

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting intercompany prices for aligner sheets or royalties that deviate from arm's length, shifting profits to low-tax jurisdictions without economic justification
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income by the tax authority; 40% penalty for lack of documentation or inaccurate documentation; interest on underpaid tax; potential criminal liability for fraudulent transfer pricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve non-arm's length transactions may be held personally liable for the resulting tax adjustments and penalties; in cases of fraud, criminal prosecution may follow

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain proper accounting records, use of undisclosed bank accounts, or involvement in money laundering through the dental aligner business (e.g., accepting cash payments without declaration)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €1 million and imprisonment up to 5 years for money laundering; administrative penalties for non-compliance with French AML regulations (e.g., failure to report suspicious transactions)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held criminally liable for AML violations; personal fines and imprisonment; travel bans and seizure of personal assets; disqualification from managing companies
